question: A research team develops a new monoclonal antibody checkpoint inhibitor for advanced melanoma that has shown promise in animal studies as well as high efficacy and low toxicity in early phase human clinical trials. The research team would now like to compare this drug to existing standard of care immunotherapy for advanced melanoma. Because the novel drug has been determined to have few side effects, this trial will offer the novel drug to patients who are deemed to be at risk for toxicity with the current standard of care immunotherapy. Which of the following best describes the level of evidence that this study can offer?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Novel monoclonal antibody checkpoint inhibitor developed -> Shown promise in animal studies -> High efficacy and low toxicity in early phase human clinical trials -> Comparing to existing standard of care immunotherapy for advanced melanoma -> Offering novel drug to patients at risk for toxicity with current standard of care -> Level 2 -> 80%
analysis: This study design falls under Level 2 evidence as it involves a randomized controlled trial comparing the novel drug to the existing standard of care immunotherapy in patients at risk for toxicity. This design allows for a more robust comparison of efficacy and safety outcomes.
